PQ and EMC problems are present in the same time in a static excitation generator system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of power quality and EMC problems at a thyristor controlled rectifier bridge, which are caused by the line voltage notches.
the measurement of power quality and EMC disturbances for a static excitor in a generator power group.
the analysis of the PQ/EMC problem at a static exciter and the development of a new compensation strategy for the notching effect.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the line notching and line current distortion are two problems with different nature.
PQ and EMC problems are not mutually exclusive.

the static excitation system is a very good solution for power system generator groups, but with the disadvantage of facing two important and interrelated problems: the line notching and the line current distortion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in order to obtain a PQ compliant excitation system, the compensation of the line voltage and line current notching is necessary, and also to avoid the electromagnetic disturbance, the compensation of line voltage and line voltage notching is necessary.
the line notching phenomenon is a problem that is not solved yet and it is a challenge for future work.
the static excitation system is not a source of electromagnetic disturbances and it does not influence the PQ parameters of the power system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the line current notching can be reduced to the acceptable levels by using the compensation strategies based on passive and active filters.
the line voltage notched by the controlled rectifier bridge can be compensated by the use of a shunt active power filter.
the harmonic distortion in the PQ domain can be compensated with a shunt filter, but the EMC domain is not affected.
